newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber extends fall at close.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber extends fall at close.

text.p: The rubber market extended its fall with prices falling further in the absence of fresh demand from consumers who continue to wait for lower levels.
"Nobody is interested in this falling market. The buyers know that prices could dip further as Malaysian prices are higher than those in Indonesia and Thailand," a dealer said.
Latex business was thin and interest came from local dealers' covering, while other grades remained weak as demand continued sluggish amid wild fluctuations in the ringgit against the U.S. dollar.

Some Far East consumers were seen checking prices at lower levels, dealers said. "Buyers are not taking up huge positions as the market is moving nearer to the INRO's may-buy level of 183," a dealer said.
INRO's five-day average was 183.56 Malaysian/Singapore cents a kg on July 9 against 185.11 cents on July 8. The daily indicator price was 181.66 against 181.84.
"We are just watching whether INRO will intervene if the five-day reaches the "may-buy" level to prop up prices," a dealer said.
Activity was mainly from hand-to-mouth basis.
